children: Bitcoin slipped below $82,000, and leveraged bulls paid for it almost immediately. Roughly $120 million in long positions across crypto were liquidated in the span of 15 minutes.

The drop pushed Bitcoin under the $82,000 mark during intraday trading on October 12. As the price fell, exchanges began forcibly closing leveraged long positions, which are bets that the price would keep rising.
That forced selling is called a liquidation. It also tends to feed on itself, because every automatic sell order adds more downward pressure on the price.
Data from platforms including CoinGlass and Hyperliquid pointed to heavy long exposure among traders heading into the move.
CoinGlass reported that long positions made up the bulk of the liquidations in recent events. Shorts, the traders betting on declines, had a considerably better afternoon.
By the latest readings, Bitcoin was changing hands in the low $82,000 range. Traders were watching a support zone between $81,300 and $82,000, a band where buyers have previously stepped in.

On October 8, Bitcoin dropped below $81,000, touching intraday lows of approximately $80,400 to $80,500. That earlier slide triggered over $1 billion in liquidations within 24 hours, mostly on the long side. A further $696 million in related liquidations came alongside it.

Compared with that, Sunday's $120 million flush looks almost restrained. The speed, though, is the notable part: the October 8 figure accumulated over a full day, while the latest one landed in a quarter of an hour.
Both declines followed a run that took Bitcoin to highs in the $85,000 to $87,000 range earlier in October. Profit-taking near the $87,000 peak helped kick off the retreat.
US spot Bitcoin ETFs reportedly saw outflows of $487 million in a single day, which removes a meaningful source of steady buying.

No significant regulatory actions or protocol changes were reported around this stretch of price action. The swings appear tied more to traders unwinding leverage than to any single fundamental headline.
After earlier sharp drops, Bitcoin has rebounded fast, at one point climbing back above $83,000.
The $81,300 to $82,000 support band is the near-term level to watch. A clean break below it could trigger another round of forced selling if traders remain heavily leveraged.
A single $487 million outflow day doesn't define a trend, but continued redemptions would mean less institutional demand absorbing the selling when leveraged traders get flushed.
The October 8 low near $80,400 also serves as a reference point. Revisiting that level would put the market back where the $1 billion-plus liquidation day bottomed out.

title: Bitcoin falls below $82,000 as $120 million in crypto longs get liquidated
